summary: Balranald Airport is a small regional airfield serving the remote outback town of Balranald in the Riverina region of New South Wales, Australia. The airport primarily supports general aviation, charter operations, and occasional emergency medical flights, serving as a vital transport link for this isolated community. Its remote location in the semi-arid landscape makes it an important gateway for visitors exploring the nearby Mungo National Park and the Willandra Lakes World Heritage Area.
faqs:
Q: Where is Balranald Airport located?
A: Balranald Airport is located approximately 6 km north of the town centre of Balranald in far western New South Wales, Australia.

Q: Does Balranald Airport have scheduled commercial flights?
A: No, the airport does not currently have regular scheduled commercial passenger service and primarily handles charter, private, and general aviation traffic.

Q: What facilities are available at Balranald Airport?
A: The airport has a sealed runway suitable for small to medium aircraft, basic infrastructure, and limited terminal facilities, as it is primarily used for general aviation.

Q: Can charter flights be arranged to and from Balranald?
A: Yes, charter and air ambulance services can be arranged, with the airport commonly used for medical evacuations and fly-in visitors heading to nearby national parks.
transport_tips: Car rental is the most practical option for reaching the airport, as the town is small and taxi services are limited. The airport is a short drive from the Balranald town centre via local roads. Visitors should arrange ground transport in advance, as there are no scheduled shuttle services operating to the airport.
local_tip: Pack your own refreshments and fuel up in town before heading to the airport, as there are no catering or fuel services for passengers on-site, and the nearest food options are back in Balranald itself.
